html:
A huge Catholic church in Barcelona, designed mostly by the Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí. Building began in 1882 and is still going on.

Another architect started it, but Gaudí took over in 1883 and made it his life's work, living on site in his last years. He mixed Gothic forms with shapes from nature: columns that branch like trees, towers like honeycombs, and facades covered in carved scenes. He planned eighteen spires. When asked about the slow pace, he is said to have answered that his client was not in a hurry. He was killed by a tram in 1926, with only a small part finished.

The work relies on donations and later on ticket sales. In the Spanish Civil War his workshop was burned and many plans and models destroyed, so later builders had to piece his design back together. Modern computers and machine cut stone have sped things up. Pope Benedict XVI consecrated it as a basilica in 2010. It is one of the most visited monuments in Spain, part of the Catalan Modernisme movement.
sum: A huge Catholic church in Barcelona, designed mostly by the Catalan architect Antoni Gaudí. Building began in 1882 and is still going on.
